newsitem.title: USA: President Mubarak arrives in Washington.
newsitem.headline: President Mubarak arrives in Washington.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak arrived in Washington on Saturday for a three-day official visit to the United States.
Mubarak's plane landed at Andrews Air Force Base in Maryland near Washington early on Saturday afternoon, an Air Force spokesman said.

Mubarak had no public events scheduled until Monday when he meets President Bill Clinton at the White House. Their talks were expected to focus on Middle East peace talks, including Israel's recent decision to build more houses for Jews in East Jerusalem.
The United States on Friday night vetoed a U.N. Security Council Resolution calling on Israel to abandon plans for the new Jewish neighbourhood in the mainly Arab section of Jerusalem.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said earlier on Friday that the Israeli actions had "gravely affected" the credibility of the Middle East peace process, creating an atmosphere of pessimism.

In a speech in Washington on the eve of Mubarak's visit, Moussa said Egypt looked to the United States to play an active role as honest broker to get the process back on track. He made clear that Egypt would be pressing Washington to take a firm line with Israel.

"We are looking forward for an active role to be played by the United States and we are ready to do the same," Moussa said. "The role of the United States as an honest broker should be promoted, should be preserved, because the role of the U.S. ... is very much a must."
